assumptions: The card's WRITE PATHS block omitted experiments/ptr-engine/tools/handoff_lint.py, but step 2 orders the EXISTING linter be extended and HANDOFF-LINT.json names that module; writing a second linter is what step 2 forbids. I edited that module additively (new functions + new codes, no existing code path altered) and proved the other codes' counts identical before/after on the live corpus.

The journal rule is applied only when <root>/orchestration/journals exists, so every pre-existing test fixture (tmp workspaces with no journal convention) keeps its exact prior behaviour; the additive proof is a test.
A torn FINAL journal line is tolerated when an earlier record is usable, matching tools/unit_journal.py (torn_lines: 1 is not fatal there); the last VALID record is what must carry step+timestamp.

Forward-only is keyed on the handoff mtime: exempt when the basename is in the frozen baseline, or the handoff is not newer than frozen_at, or it was written inside a 180s in-flight grace window (sibling units write handoffs concurrently). The live corpus grew 1023 -> 1031 handoffs during this unit and produced 0 new misses.
A unit card with no handoff is invisible to the rule by construction; the test counts them (7 at the last run) rather than pretending they are covered.

limit: A linter that runs in a unit's own test suite cannot police a unit that never runs it -- the unit that writes no journal is exactly the unit that skips the suite. The alternative is a board-side pre-handoff hook that refuses to settle a card whose journal is absent; it needs operator approval this workspace cannot grant.
